test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 17 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A well with an internal diameter 10 m is dug to a depth of 10 m. Earth taken out of it is spread all around the well to a width of 12 m to form an embankment. What is the height (in m, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of the embankment?
solution:
**Given:**

Internal diameter of the well (d) = 10 m

Internal radius of the well (r) = d / 2 = 10 / 2 = 5 m

Depth of the well (h) = 10 m

Width of the embankment = 12 m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of earth taken out from the well (cylinder) = pi r² h

Outer radius of the embankment (R) = Internal radius of the well + Width of the embankment

Area of the embankment (circular ring) = pi (R² - r²)

Volume of the embankment (cylinder) = Area of the embankment × Height of the embankment

Volume of earth taken out = Volume of the embankment
